findings.asked: Make a variable the subject when it is squared inside a formula.
findings.wentWrong: Square roots were taken before dividing by A, or the root sign covered only the numerator; some started with B - A.
findings.rule: Isolate the squared term completely, then root the whole of both sides.

findings.asked: Change the subject of a formula.
findings.wentWrong: Over 20% could not even divide both sides by A.
findings.rule: Undo operations in reverse order, one per line.

findings.asked: Make x the subject when x appears twice.
findings.wentWrong: Few finished; a mark for reaching 4y = 5x - vx; many had no idea x had to be collected and left it on both sides.
findings.fullMarkAnswersDid: Collected the x terms on one side, factorised x out, divided by the bracket.

findings.asked: Change the subject where the subject appears twice.
findings.wentWrong: Under half full marks; over a third never gathered the x terms to one side.
findings.rule: First move: every term containing the subject to one side.

findings.asked: Binary conversion, then change the subject.
findings.wentWrong: Steps were skipped; a mark was available for the intermediate line 3m = h - y.

ruleToRemember: Collect every term containing the subject on one side, factorise the subject out, divide by the bracket; undo powers last, applying the root to the whole side.
aStarSignal: A formula with the subject appearing twice and inside a power, rearranged in a clean sequence of single steps.
